name: 2.5D Parallax Animation, in the Motion Design and Cinematography category. The label was normalized from source descriptions, so it is not a canonical name.
visualIdentity: Flat artwork is separated into foreground, midground, and background layers with plausible depth and occlusion. Layers move at restrained relative speeds, with extra artwork kept beyond the crop. Layered parallax does not prove full 3D modeling.
suitableUses: Explicitly listed good fits are 3D dioramas and miniature sets, isometric scenes with constrained movement, and layered illustration, paper craft, collage, or 2.5D artwork. Storybook explainers and historical documentaries are inferred from the suggested hybrids, not confirmed for this style.
limitations: Avoid reversed depth motion, exposed edges, and excessive layer separation. Adapt or omit the style when camera tilt breaks isometric projection, when movement exposes incomplete layers or breaks ground contact, or when depth hides essential labels. Source-supplied audio requirements are unspecified.
palette: This is a reference-dependent example applying only to new presentation elements. Suggested tokens are background #EFE7D6, foreground #34473F, and accent_1 #8A9C85, with no gradient. Task or brand colors override them, and source artwork colors must stay unchanged. Foreground on background measures 8.056:1, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target. Accent_1 under foreground text measures 3.386:1, so it is decorative only. Recheck composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Motion uses a shared camera transform plus measured per-layer offsets driven by deterministic composition time. The source specifies no easing values or timing. Three optional motion references exist: motion-009 for depth-dependent pointer parallax, motion-012 for progress-controlled chapter handoffs, and motion-015 for narrative steps. None is required, and video must not depend on live input.
audio: The source gives no mandatory audio layer, genre, tempo, or voice. Suggested options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen by topic and audience. Explicit user audio choices and supplied assets come first. When inputs are absent, state assumptions and keep speech intelligible without clipping.
assetRequirements: Layers should be prepared as PNG or SVG with alpha, consistent dimensions, clear naming, and a layer manifest or numbered frames, then inspected before composition. Each layer needs overscan beyond the crop for parallax travel. Cropper.js is optional for crop authoring but does not separate layers, remove backgrounds, or reconstruct hidden pixels. Creature assets apply only to the optional motion-009 hop.
combinations: The source states that 2.5D parallax needs artwork, so a hybrid is recommended. Suggested pairing one is style-030 storybook scene plates, using a primary earthy palette and overscan while avoiding excessive separation. Suggested pairing two is style-044 period photo cutouts, tinted to palette tokens with consistent grain and no invented archival assets. Both are suggestions, not verified.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, sync, validation, and export, with a paused seekable GSAP timeline registered per composition. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and that reason must be recorded. Visuals use PixiJS, native DOM/SVG, or Three.js only for true 3D. Producers must verify direct and sequential seeks, frames, audio sync, and loop seams.
